newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends down on good liquidity, gilts up.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends down on good liquidity, gilts up.

text.p: Indian call money eased on lack of demand to end Tuesday at 2.75-3.0 percent, off opening quotes of 4.0-4.25 percent, dealers said.
They said good funds supply and poor demand pushed rates down. Call money is expected to remain easy through the week unless liquidity is drained away by a government bond issue, they said.

"The market is largely sentiment-driven," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "With inflows of around 56 billion rupees expected before July 18, sentiment has improved. Rates will remain easy unless a bond issue is announced."
Dealers said prices of government securities were mixed in active trade, with two-way movement.
"Prices rose in the morning, then fell before going up again in the afternoon," said a dealer. "Most of the action remains in medium-term securities."

The 12.59 percent 2004 traded on Tuesday between 101.06 and 101.27 rupees against Monday's 101.20, the zero-coupon 2000 bond at 72.45 to 72.55 against 72.35 while the 12.14 percent 2000 at 102.05-102.10 against 102.12, dealers said.
Among other stocks, the 12 percent 1999 rose to 102.85 from 102.75 and the 13.65 percent 2002 to 104.70 from 104.66.
Dealers said the 364-day treasury bill maturing on July 9, 1998 traded at a yield of 8.5 percent and the April 10 bill at 8.38 percent.
